## Stage and working tree

- **Stage:** P5 "Configuration automation and outputs", gate DG5 (BUILDING).
- **Working tree:** a separate git worktree prepared by the orchestrator. It is your current working directory (`--cwd`), on branch `dg5/be-e2`, at the integrated `HEAD`.
  - `node_modules` is installed and the packages are built.
  - Work only in this tree. Never run `git worktree add`.
- **Concurrency (D-004):** Four W13 tasks run at the same time (BE-P2, BE-E2, KBE-D2, BE-O), each in its own worktree; no architecture task runs. W1–W12 are merged (D-157). Stay strictly inside your file ownership.
- **Preceding gate:** run `node tools/gates/validate.mjs --historical --stage DG4` first, and report the result. It must exit 0.
- **Time:** the hard limit is about 2 hours. Run `date -u` at the start and at the end.
  - Work in the order your section gives.
  - If you pass about 100 minutes, finish the current item, make the tree typecheck and lint, and write the handback, listing exactly what remains. Name its separable second half if your section gives one (D-059/D-070).

## Binding scope

- **Your section:** `docs/architecture/p5-work-split.md` §B.4. It gives your file ownership, consumed contracts, requirement rows and integration notes. Follow it exactly.
- **The shared rules:** `p5-work-split.md` §2. Reviewers check every one of them.
- **The design:** the ADRs your section cites (ADR-0039 onward, and the DG1–DG4 ADRs they extend), `docs/api/openapi.yaml`, and the zod mirrors.
- **Decisions:** D-141 to D-143 in `docs/delivery/decisions.md` (D-142 decides p5-plan Q1–Q12). Read them verbatim.
- **Pending operations:** move each operation you route out of your `apps/api/test/support/p5-pending-*.ts` list. Exercise it in your `p5-exercises-*.ts` so `contract.test.ts` stays green.
- **Acceptance texts:** the `acceptance` text of every requirement row your section assigns to you (`docs/delivery/requirements.csv`) is binding, and reviewers test it literally. A row that cites a later-stage A-test is judged on its own acceptance text (D-142).
- **User-facing text** must be true for the release it ships in (F-DG4-160): when your work ships a feature that an existing en/ar string calls planned or later, correct that string in both languages, or list it in your handback for the owner of that file.
- **Gates:** product gates G1–G6 are business approvals inside the product. No agent grants a real business, Finance or IT approval. Seed and demo data are synthetic.
- **No new dependency.** If you need one, write the need in your handback with its official documentation, support window and licence; the orchestrator decides and installs it (D-142 Q8).

## Environment

- **Node:** 24.21.0 at `/opt/nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin`. Run offline.
- **Browser:** Chromium is pre-installed (`PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/pw-browsers`). Never run `playwright install`.
- **Your harness ports are 24800–24849 only.** Use them for `QA_PG_PORT`, `E2E_PG_PORT`, `E2E_API_PORT` and `MTH_PORT_POOL`.
- **Before tests:** remove any empty `.claude/.cc-writes` directories inside source folders.
- **Tests:** deterministic under load (F-DG4-143 to F-DG4-148); never read whole delivery folders (D-138); never stop processes with `pkill -f` or `pgrep -f`.
- **The write guard forbids editing:**
  - `tools/gates/**`, `tools/agents/**` and `.claude/**`;
  - `docs/source/**`;
  - review and gate records, `stages.json` and `findings.json`;
  - `trading_agent/`.

## Acceptance (real output in the handback)

1. These all exit 0:
   - `pnpm -r typecheck`
   - `pnpm -r build`
   - `pnpm lint`
   - `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard -z | xargs -0 npx prettier --check --ignore-unknown`
   - `pnpm openapi:lint`
2. `pnpm test` passes with the locale unset and with `C.UTF-8`, in every Vitest invocation it runs. Report the counts.
3. `QA_PG_PORT=<port> MTH_PORT_POOL=<rest> tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh pnpm test:integration` passes. Report the counts and any pinned-count change.
4. `node tools/gates/validate.mjs --historical --stage DG4` exits 0.

## Evidence honesty

Report every command with its real exit code. Disclose and explain every non-zero exit, failed or flaky test, or timeout in the logs you cite. Never report a check as passed that did not run.

## Handback

Write `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG5/T-DG5-BE-E2-backend-workflow-engineer.md`, with logs under `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG5/T-DG5-BE-E2-evidence/`. Include:
- the files changed;
- the behaviour delivered, per requirement row, quoting its acceptance text;
- the checks, with exit codes and counts;
- the operations you routed, as a delta to your pending list;
- any contract, schema or dependency need, for the orchestrator;
- the user-facing texts your work made untrue, and what you did about each;
- what remains.

Leave your changes **uncommitted** for the orchestrator to integrate.

# Agent operating protocol (shared by all project agents)

This file is mandatory reading for every project agent in `.claude/agents/`. It condenses section 0 of `docs/source/master-prompt-v2.0.md`. Where they differ, the master prompt wins.

## Two gate systems: never mix them

- **DG0–DG7** are *software delivery gates* for the engineering team. Their records live in `docs/delivery/`.
- **G1–G6** are *business transformation approvals inside the product* (Case for Change … Sustain). They are product features.
- An engineering agent can never grant a real business, Finance or IT production approval. A demo Sponsor approval in seed data approves nothing real.
- Product gate G6 (Sustain) never implies that engineering gate DG7 has passed, and DG7 never implies any G1–G6 business approval.

## Sources of truth

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Authoritative methodology (playbook v1.0) | `docs/source/playbook.md` (block anchors `B0001`–`B0165`); original `docs/source/Business_Transformation_Playbook.docx` |
| Product and delivery requirements | `docs/source/master-prompt-v2.0.md` (sections §0–§21) |
| Requirement register | `docs/delivery/requirements.csv` |
| Stage state and candidates | `docs/delivery/stages.json`, `docs/delivery/candidates/` |
| Decisions and assumptions | `docs/delivery/decisions.md` |
| Findings | `docs/delivery/findings.json` |
| Reviews / gates | `docs/delivery/reviews/DGx/round-N/`, `docs/delivery/gates/DGx.json` |
| Gate rules (validator) | `tools/gates/` (implementers must not edit it) |

## Assignment contract (what every delegation contains)

Every assignment names: stage ID; task and requirement IDs; exact source/reference files; candidate/base revision; permitted files; constraints; input/output contracts; acceptance checks; dependency status; and the expected handback path. If any of these is missing or contradictory, say so in your handback. Do not guess.

Verify the starting revision (`git rev-parse HEAD`, and `git status`) before you write anything. Do not assume your workspace contains the latest integration candidate.

## Implementation handback contract

Write your handback to the path given in the assignment (default `docs/delivery/handbacks/<stage>/<task-id>-<role>.md`). It must contain:

1. **Changed files**, with a one-line purpose for each.
2. **Behaviour delivered**, per requirement ID.
3. **Checks actually run**: exact command, environment, and the actual result or exit status. Paste the relevant output tail.
4. **Known gaps / not done**, stated plainly. An unfinished task is unfinished even if everything else went well.
5. **Merge instructions** (migrations to run, ordering, conflicts to expect).

Never report a check as passed if you did not run it. If a tool, credential or service is missing, report the check as **BLOCKED** with the exact reason.

## Review record contract (reviewers and auditor)

Reviewers write one JSON record to `docs/delivery/reviews/<DGx>/round-<N>/<role>.json`. Create it and your sidecars **only with the Write/Edit tools**, never through the shell: the validator binds each of them to the content your run's own **successful** Write/Edit calls produce when replayed from your transcript (D-021). A file you also modify through the shell no longer matches, and is rejected. They're write-once, so never edit a file from an earlier round. The record goes that conforms to `tools/gates/schemas/review.schema.json`, plus an optional Markdown narrative next to it. Required fields: `stage_id`, `candidate_id`, `source_commit`, `reviewer_role`, `invocation_reference`, `implementation_author`, `independence_declaration`, `requirements_checked`, `checks_run[]` (each with `procedure`, `command` where applicable, `environment`, `expected`, `actual`, `exit_status`, `result`), `findings[]` (finding IDs), `verdict` (PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED), `evidence_paths[]`, `reviewed_at`.

- Inspect the frozen candidate directly: source, diffs, rendered screens, running behaviour. An implementer's summary is not evidence.
- Form your verdict **before** reading any other reviewer's conclusions for the same round.
- For your `invocation_reference`, copy exactly the value the orchestrator gives you. Never invent run IDs.
- A reviewer must not have authored any implementation in the reviewed scope. If you did, declare it and return BLOCKED.
- Anything you cannot check: record it as BLOCKED with the reason. Never write PASS by default.
- Every evidence entry (in `evidence_paths`, a check's `evidence` or a verification's `evidence`) must be an existing regular file in the repository, optionally followed by `#fragment`. Directories and annotated strings are rejected by the validator.

## Findings contract

Each finding gets a stable ID `F-<DGx>-<NNN>` (the orchestrator allocates numbers; propose them in your record as `F-<DGx>-<role-prefix>-<n>` if you have none yet). Each one records: requirement ID, severity, reproduction, expected vs actual, evidence, and `mandatory_violation` (true if it breaks a mandatory requirement, data integrity, calculation accuracy, access control or deployment portability).

| Severity | Use for |
|---|---|
| Critical | Exploitable severe security flaw, data loss, fundamentally invalid financial results |
| High | Broken required workflow, major integrity failure |
| Medium | Material defect with limited scope |
| Low | Optional polish |

A severity label never overrides the mandatory-requirement rule. An author never closes their own finding. Only the originating reviewer or another qualified non-author verifies a fix.

A finding closes only through a reviewer-authored `<role>.verifications.json` sidecar in a review round. A Low, non-mandatory finding can be accepted as an observation only when both the reporting specialist (or another specialist) and the release-auditor add an entry `{"finding_id", "result": "PASS", "status_after": "ACCEPTED_OBSERVATION", "note": "<rationale>"}` to their own sidecars. The sidecar's **latest** entry for the finding decides, and it's bound to that reviewer's own run for the round. The orchestrator mirrors it into `findings.json` with `tools/gates/import-findings.mjs`, and the validator checks that the two match (D-018).

## Write scopes (mechanically enforced)

`tools/agents/guard-write.mjs` runs as a PreToolUse hook on Write/Edit for every project agent and enforces `tools/agents/write-scopes.json`:

- Reviewers write only review records and evidence.
- `qa-verifier` may also write tests under `tests/qa/**` and `e2e/**`.
  - **Before the candidate freezes:** test-first acceptance tests go there and become part of the candidate.
  - **During a review of a frozen candidate:** new tests go under `docs/delivery/test-evidence/<DGx>/qa/tests/`, so they don't alter the candidate. The orchestrator promotes them into `tests/qa/` in the next stage.
- Implementers cannot write gate rules, agent definitions, source documents, reviews, gate records or `stages.json`.

Your whole agent process runs in a kernel-enforced sandbox (bubblewrap; D-030), and your Bash commands run in a second one nested inside it (D-025). Writes outside your role's areas fail with "Read-only file system", **whether you use the shell or the file tools**.

- **Confined roles** (reviewers, auditor, analyst): anything created at the repository's top level is thrown away when the run ends.
- **Review records, the gate record and the analyst's register** are written to a private staging copy. After your run the runner copies back only your own new `round-N/<your-role>.*` files, the auditor's `<DGx>.json` and the analyst's `requirements.csv`. It reports anything else, and a run with such writes is not committed.
- **Visibility:** you don't see records that other reviewers write during your run.
- **HOME** is read-only.

The shell sandbox's details follow. Shell writes to protected paths fail with "Read-only file system": git metadata, Claude configuration, gate and agent tooling, sources, delivery records, and for reviewers and the analyst everything outside their own areas. The sandbox has **no network access**. For a disposable copy of the candidate use `git clone <repo> "$TMPDIR/<name>"`. Inside the sandbox only your run's own `$TMPDIR` is writable scratch. The runner creates a private directory for every run (`/var/tmp/mth-run.*`, exported as `TMPDIR` and `MTH_RUN_TMP`), so no other agent can reach your disposable clones, and it removes it when the run ends. `/tmp` and `/var/tmp` themselves are read-only. Keep anything that must survive the run in your evidence directory (D-028).

**Your evidence directory.** Each reviewer writes evidence only under `docs/delivery/test-evidence/<DGx>/<key>/`, where the key is `domain`, `code-security`, `qa` or `audit`. It writes review files only as `docs/delivery/reviews/<DGx>/round-<N>/<your-role>.*`. The write guard and the sandbox both refuse other reviewers' records and evidence (F-DG0-144). A reproduction must never touch another agent's files or scratch. `git worktree add` needs write access to `.git` and is denied. The runner also checks configuration surfaces before and after your run (D-024/D-025). Reviewers who execute code must do so in a disposable copy: a temporary clone under `$TMPDIR`, or a throwaway database or container. Never do it in the candidate tree.

## Honesty rules

- Do not label planned features as delivered. Do not fabricate provenance, test results, run IDs, approvals, screenshots or evidence.
- Record demonstration data as synthetic.
- Do not claim PMI certification, official Mobily brand compliance or regulatory compliance.
- `#0078FF` is a provisional brand token, not a verified Mobily colour.

## Infrastructure: permission-classifier outages

Your shell runs in the permission mode `auto`. Sometimes the server-side classifier returns no verdict, and a command is refused with "classifier gave no verdict" or "Classifier unavailable". That's a transient infrastructure failure, not a judgement about your action.

- **Retry a refused command.** Retry up to 3 times, and keep working on non-shell parts of the task in between.
- **If you still can't run what the task needs, stop cleanly.** End your turn with a final message whose **first line is exactly** `CLASSIFIER-BLOCKED`, followed by what's done and what's pending. The runner then resumes the **same session** (same invocation reference) after a pause, up to 6 times, and you continue from where you stopped.
- **Never report a check as passed that didn't run.**

Required fields: `stage_id`, `candidate_id`, `source_commit`, `reviewer_role`, `invocation_reference`, `implementation_author`, `independence_declaration`, `requirements_checked`, `checks_run[]` (each with `procedure`, `command` where applicable, `environment`, `expected`, `actual`, `exit_status`, `result`), `findings[]` (finding IDs), `verdict` (PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED), `evidence_paths[]`, `reviewed_at`.

- Inspect the frozen candidate directly: source, diffs, rendered screens, running behaviour. An implementer's summary is not evidence.
- Form your verdict **before** reading any other reviewer's conclusions for the same round.
- For your `invocation_reference`, copy exactly the value the orchestrator gives you. Never invent run IDs.
- A reviewer must not have authored any implementation in the reviewed scope. If you did, declare it and return BLOCKED.
- Anything you cannot check: record it as BLOCKED with the reason. Never write PASS by default.
- Every evidence entry (in `evidence_paths`, a check's `evidence` or a verification's `evidence`) must be an existing regular file in the repository, optionally followed by `#fragment`. Directories and annotated strings are rejected by the validator.

## Findings contract

Each finding gets a stable ID `F-<DGx>-<NNN>` (the orchestrator allocates numbers; propose them in your record as `F-<DGx>-<role-prefix>-<n>` if you have none yet). Each one records: requirement ID, severity, reproduction, expected vs actual, evidence, and `mandatory_violation` (true if it breaks a mandatory requirement, data integrity, calculation accuracy, access control or deployment portability).

| Severity | Use for |
|---|---|
| Critical | Exploitable severe security flaw, data loss, fundamentally invalid financial results |
| High | Broken required workflow, major integrity failure |
| Medium | Material defect with limited scope |
| Low | Optional polish |

A severity label never overrides the mandatory-requirement rule. An author never closes their own finding. Only the originating reviewer or another qualified non-author verifies a fix.

A finding closes only through a reviewer-authored `<role>.verifications.json` sidecar in a review round. A Low, non-mandatory finding can be accepted as an observation only when both the reporting specialist (or another specialist) and the release-auditor add an entry `{"finding_id", "result": "PASS", "status_after": "ACCEPTED_OBSERVATION", "note": "<rationale>"}` to their own sidecars. The sidecar's **latest** entry for the finding decides, and it's bound to that reviewer's own run for the round. The orchestrator mirrors it into `findings.json` with `tools/gates/import-findings.mjs`, and the validator checks that the two match (D-018).

## Write scopes (mechanically enforced)

`tools/agents/guard-write.mjs` runs as a PreToolUse hook on Write/Edit for every project agent and enforces `tools/agents/write-scopes.json`:

- Reviewers write only review records and evidence.
- `qa-verifier` may also write tests under `tests/qa/**` and `e2e/**`.
  - **Before the candidate freezes:** test-first acceptance tests go there and become part of the candidate.
  - **During a review of a frozen candidate:** new tests go under `docs/delivery/test-evidence/<DGx>/qa/tests/`, so they don't alter the candidate. The orchestrator promotes them into `tests/qa/` in the next stage.
- Implementers cannot write gate rules, agent definitions, source documents, reviews, gate records or `stages.json`.

Your whole agent process runs in a kernel-enforced sandbox (bubblewrap; D-030), and your Bash commands run in a second one nested inside it (D-025). Writes outside your role's areas fail with "Read-only file system", **whether you use the shell or the file tools**.

- **Confined roles** (reviewers, auditor, analyst): anything created at the repository's top level is thrown away when the run ends.
- **Review records, the gate record and the analyst's register** are written to a private staging copy. After your run the runner copies back only your own new `round-N/<your-role>.*` files, the auditor's `<DGx>.json` and the analyst's `requirements.csv`. It reports anything else, and a run with such writes is not committed.
- **Visibility:** you don't see records that other reviewers write during your run.
- **HOME** is read-only.

The shell sandbox's details follow. Shell writes to protected paths fail with "Read-only file system": git metadata, Claude configuration, gate and agent tooling, sources, delivery records, and for reviewers and the analyst everything outside their own areas. The sandbox has **no network access**. For a disposable copy of the candidate use `git clone <repo> "$TMPDIR/<name>"`. Inside the sandbox only your run's own `$TMPDIR` is writable scratch. The runner creates a private directory for every run (`/var/tmp/mth-run.*`, exported as `TMPDIR` and `MTH_RUN_TMP`), so no other agent can reach your disposable clones, and it removes it when the run ends. `/tmp` and `/var/tmp` themselves are read-only. Keep anything that must survive the run in your evidence directory (D-028).

**Your evidence directory.** Each reviewer writes evidence only under `docs/delivery/test-evidence/<DGx>/<key>/`, where the key is `domain`, `code-security`, `qa` or `audit`. It writes review files only as `docs/delivery/reviews/<DGx>/round-<N>/<your-role>.*`. The write guard and the sandbox both refuse other reviewers' records and evidence (F-DG0-144). A reproduction must never touch another agent's files or scratch. `git worktree add` needs write access to `.git` and is denied. The runner also checks configuration surfaces before and after your run (D-024/D-025). Reviewers who execute code must do so in a disposable copy: a temporary clone under `$TMPDIR`, or a throwaway database or container. Never do it in the candidate tree.

## Honesty rules

- Do not label planned features as delivered. Do not fabricate provenance, test results, run IDs, approvals, screenshots or evidence.
- Record demonstration data as synthetic.
- Do not claim PMI certification, official Mobily brand compliance or regulatory compliance.
- `#0078FF` is a provisional brand token, not a verified Mobily colour.

## Infrastructure: permission-classifier outages

Your shell runs in the permission mode `auto`. Sometimes the server-side classifier returns no verdict, and a command is refused with "classifier gave no verdict" or "Classifier unavailable". That's a transient infrastructure failure, not a judgement about your action.

- **Retry a refused command.** Retry up to 3 times, and keep working on non-shell parts of the task in between.
- **If you still can't run what the task needs, stop cleanly.** End your turn with a final message whose **first line is exactly** `CLASSIFIER-BLOCKED`, followed by what's done and what's pending. The runner then resumes the **same session** (same invocation reference) after a pause, up to 6 times, and you continue from where you stopped.
- **Never report a check as passed that didn't run.**

# P5 work split: shared rules, file ownership, contracts and integration order

- **Plan:** `docs/architecture/p5-plan.md` (T-DG5-ARCH-00), adopted by D-142 with the orchestrator's decisions on Q1–Q12. This file holds one section per architecture task (p5-plan §4); each ARCH task writes only its own section. §1–§2 and §A are written by T-DG5-ARCH-01; §B+C by T-DG5-ARCH-02, §D+E by T-DG5-ARCH-03, §F by T-DG5-ARCH-04, §G+H by T-DG5-ARCH-05, §I+J by T-DG5-ARCH-06.
- **Stage:** P5 "Configuration automation and outputs" (DG5).
- **Rule:** two tasks never edit the same file (REQ-DLV-008). Anything not listed under an owner is **frozen**; changes go through the orchestrator (p5-plan §5.3).
- **Off-limits to every implementer** (the write guard enforces it): `tools/gates/**`, `tools/agents/**`, `.claude/**`, `docs/source/**`, `docs/delivery/reviews/**`, `docs/delivery/gates/**`, `docs/delivery/stages.json`, `docs/delivery/findings.json`, `trading_agent/`.
- **Product gates G1–G6 are business approvals inside the product.** Nothing in P5 reads or writes the engineering gate records DG0–DG7. Product G6 never implies DG7, and no agent, seed or job grants a real business, Finance or IT approval. Demo approvals are synthetic and labelled so.

## 1. How to read a slice section

Each slice section lists: what the architect already delivered (do not re-create); one block per implementer task with its exact files, the operations it routes, the contracts it consumes and its tests; the migrations left in the slice range and their order; the integration order; a requirement → owner table; and what the implementers must know. Paths are relative to `apps/api/src/modules/` unless they start with `apps/`, `packages/`, `docs/` or `tests/`. Every task also owns its tests, its `apps/api/test/support/p5-pending-<task>.ts` and its `apps/api/test/integration/contract/p5-exercises-<task>.ts`.

## 2. Shared rules for every P5 implementer task (the DG2–DG4 lessons; reviewers check them)

1. **Free text.** Every free-text field goes through the shared `freeText`/`hasText`/`hasInvalidCharacter` rules; truncation only through `truncateText`.
2. **Strict UTF-8.** JSON and query parsing is strict UTF-8 on every route (the BE13 parser); no route-local parser.
3. **`config.consumes`.** Every new route's `config.consumes` equals its operation's request media type in `docs/api/openapi.yaml` (every slice A body is `application/json`; bodiless action POSTs declare none).

- **Tests (REQ-S05-001 literal, T01 and T14):** after an edit, history lists the new version with the changed fields; a comment and a reply persist and read back; a reply to a reply → 422 `form_comment.parent_invalid`; an attachment on T14 (`benefit`, `form_record_attachment`) and on T01 (`diagnostic_item`, `evidence_link`) persist and list; removal needs a reason; AUD 403 on writes; free-text rules on comment bodies.

### B.4 BE-E2 — export, bulk edit, drafts, the recoverable conflict (backend-workflow-engineer; after BE-E)

- **Files:** `forms/export.ts` (CSV RFC 4180 UTF-8 with BOM and JSON; 5000-row cap), `forms/bulk.ts` (all-or-nothing through each register's exported update function; a register without one is listed in the handback and its record type stays `bulk_edit_allowed` only if served), `forms/drafts.ts`, the `transformations/register-kit.ts` lines that expose each register's update function to `forms/bulk.ts` (named lines only; existing routes unchanged), their `forms/routes.ts` lines, tests.
- **Operations (7):** `exportFormRecords`, `bulkUpdateFormRecords`, `listFormDrafts`, `createFormDraft`, `getFormDraft`, `updateFormDraft`, `closeFormDraft`.
- **Consumes:** ADR-0041 §5–§7, §10; `config.consumes` `application/json` on every body; the export response declares `text/csv` and `application/json`.
- **Tests (REQ-S05-001 literal, T01 and T14):** a saved draft reopens with its payload and `baseChanged` after a concurrent edit; export returns the rows (CSV and JSON, en and ar headers; Unknown marked, never 0); bulk edit of owners on 3 T15 records commits all, and with one stale version commits none (409 `form_record.bulk_conflict` listing it); a conflicting concurrent save returns the recoverable 409; AUD 403; one audit event per record written.

### B.5 Migrations of slice B and C

`0068`–`0070` are delivered. **`0071`–`0073`** are free and are taken, in this order, only by a slice B/C task whose handback shows a database need: **`0071` BE-F2** (expected: the work-item kind `procedure_step` and its My Work section line, if the step assignment is shown in My Work — ADR-0042 §7); **`0072` BE-G** (only if an output adapter needs a constraint or seed change); **`0073` BE-E2** (only if bulk edit or export needs one). A task that needs none leaves its number unused; numbers are never reordered.

### B.6 Integration order (slice B)

ARCH-02 → KBE-B → BE-D (after BE-A) → BE-E → BE-E2 → FE-C (form-builder screens and the form framework on T01 and T14; p5-plan §5.1). BE-E and BE-E2 are sequential on `forms/routes.ts`.

### B.7 Requirement → owner (slice B)

| Requirement | Owner task(s) | Completes with |
|---|---|---|
| REQ-S05-001 | BE-E (history, comments, attachments), BE-E2 (drafts, export, bulk, conflict), BE-D (validation, inline help reads) | FE-C (T01 and T14 screens) |
| REQ-S05-002 | BE-D (provider, protected columns) | FE-C (Studio fields screen) |
| REQ-S05-006 | BE-D (registry reads, badge) | FE-C (badge in en and ar on the twelve forms); the twelve creates/reads are the DG2–DG4 operations of ADR-0041 §1 and BE-F's `putProcedureDefinition` |
| REQ-S06-005 | KBE-B (validators), BE-D (wiring, calculated fields) | — |
| REQ-S16-010 | BE-D (custom values) | — |

### C.6 What the implementers of slices B and C must know

1. **One key per kind.** Form schemas are kind `form_schema`, key `forms`; procedures are kind `procedure`, key `procedures`. Drafts copy every row of their base (ADR-0039 §2); the content hash includes the provider rows (ADR-0042 §1), so recompute it on every write.
2. **The database refuses what the ADRs refuse.** API checks come first and return the ADR-0041 §10 / ADR-0042 §10 codes; reaching a `0068`/`0069` guard is a programming error. The probe (`probe-output.txt`) names each guard and its constraint name.
3. **Decimals.** Every number, percentage and currency value is a decimal string (KBE-B validators); a percentage is stored as a fraction; currency carries its code. Unknown and Not computable are never 0 or green.
4. **No DG2–DG4 change.** Custom values live in `form_custom_value`; attachments of the twenty DG2 record types stay in `evidence_link`; bulk edits and output adapters call the owning modules' existing services. Any change to a DG2–DG4 route, request, response or rule is a reopen candidate: stop and raise it.
5. **Pins.** DG1–DG4 transformations resolve to forms v1 (no back-fill); new ones are pinned at creation by BE-D's initializer. A running procedure instance stays on its definition version.
6. **Approvals.** Procedure approval steps are decided only through the canonical approval by the human business approver; tests use synthetic approvers labelled as such.
7. **Locks.** 730254 for instance step transitions; no lock for comments (append-only); 730255–730257 stay reserved.
8. **Exactly once.** Automation launches carry `launch_key` (UNIQUE); work items use `createWorkItemOnce` with `procedure_step:<stepInstanceId>:<kind>`.
9. **D-142 decisions** are binding: Q1 (stable identities), Q4 ("create" for TOMDimension = a draft element), Q8 (no new dependency).

1	# ADR-0041: Form schema versions, the eleven Studio field types, extension fields and protected source columns, custom-field values validated against the pinned version, the common form framework, and the twelve extension record types
2	
3	- **Status:** Proposed for P5 (DG5). Author: solution-architect (T-DG5-ARCH-02), 2026-10-14.
4	- **Requirements (slice B of `docs/architecture/p5-plan.md`):** REQ-S05-001, REQ-S05-002, REQ-S05-006, REQ-S06-005, REQ-S16-010. It also supplies the "fields and validation" part of REQ-S06-004 and the "added field" diff rows of REQ-S06-007 that ADR-0039 §4 assigns to this slice, and the "new required field" provider of REQ-S06-008 (ADR-0040).
5	- **Sources (quoted where a design point has one):**
6	  - M0127 (§5): "Implement every numbered template as a native structured form/register. Preserve all source columns below; extensions may add fields without deleting their meaning. Include inline help, validation, draft saving, version history, comments, attachments, permissions, bulk editing where suitable and export."
7	  - M0128–M0144 (§5): the table of the sixteen templates and their "Minimum fields or content".
8	  - M0145–M0148 (§5): the Charter, the TOM Canvas and the Business Case as "first-class native records".
9	  - M0149 (§5): "Native operating records added for execution. Structured evidence, baseline registry, value-pool register, resource/capacity plan, funding approvals, process/procedure definitions, change requests, meeting records, corrective plans, lessons learned, BAU handover and controls. Mark these as extensions where the source does not supply a full template."
10	  - M0150 (§5): "… Avoid duplicate registers that drift."
11	  - M0154 (§6): "Include field types for text, rich text, number, currency, percentage, date, reference, attachment, lookup, choice and calculated value. Protect stable system identifiers and core data invariants."
12	  - M0155 (§6): "Existing transformations remain pinned to their methodology and form versions until a deliberate migration is approved."
13	  - M0315 (§16): "Use typed relational tables for core entities and validated metadata/JSON structures for extensible custom fields and versioned forms. Avoid a single unvalidated JSON blob as the entire database."
14	  - Playbook template blocks: B0030 (T1), B0049 (T2), B0057 (T3), B0064 (T4), B0071 (T5), B0075 (T6), B0078 (T7), B0080 (T8), B0086 (T9), B0094 (T10), B0098 (T11), B0100 (T12), B0106 (T13), B0122 (T14), B0127 (T15), B0129 (T16) — the `source_element` template labels (0064).
15	- **Decisions applied:** D-141, D-142 (**Q1** stable identities and version-scoped rows; **Q8** no new dependency), D-143 (ARCH-01 integrated), D-088 §2 and F-DG3-100 (claims enumerated and exactly true).
16	- **Builds on:** ADR-0003 (optimistic concurrency), ADR-0004 (audit), ADR-0006 (authorization), ADR-0007 (API conventions, §5b statuses), ADR-0014 §4 (custom fields; amended here, §4), ADR-0016 (P2 guards, lock registry), ADR-0018 (evidence and `evidence_link`), ADR-0024 (formula engine, unchanged), ADR-0039 (Studio kinds, `methodology_element`, `ConfigResolver`, publish pipeline), ADR-0040 (migration of pins).
17	- **Physical model:** `0068_p5_form_schemas_framework.sql`, `0070_p5_forms_procedures_permissions_coverage.sql` (permissions). Probe ids (FS, FE, CV, FD, FC, FA, PM, G) refer to `docs/delivery/handbacks/DG5/T-DG5-ARCH-02-evidence/probe-output.txt`.
18	- **Two gate systems.** Product gates G1–G6 are business approvals inside the product. Nothing here reads or writes DG0–DG7. A form schema review is a configuration review, not a business approval.
19	
20	## Context
21	
22	As built on `HEAD` `7344b25` (DG4 APPROVED; slice A integrated, D-143):
23	
24	1. The sixteen templates, the Charter, the TOM canvas, the business case and the M0149 records are typed DG2–DG4 tables with their own routes (e.g. `tom_gap`, `benefit`, `raid_entry`, `evidence`, `lesson`). No migration `0001`–`0064` creates a `custom_field_values` column, although ADR-0014 §4 says custom fields "live in `custom_field_values jsonb` columns".
25	2. Several of those tables have immutability or frozen-column triggers (e.g. `funding_decision` has no `version` and is append-only; `evidence` and `decision` freeze columns after review or decision).
26	3. `evidence_link` (`0012`) attaches evidence to twenty DG2 record types through `p2_record_ref_guard`.
27	4. Slice A declared the `form_schema` configuration kind (`0062`) but no element type for it: `methodology_element_guard` refused every element of that kind.
28	5. The audit trail (`audit_event`, `0003`) records every mutation of every guarded table with `prior_version`/`new_version` and a `changes` object; it is the existing version history.
29	
30	## Decision
31	
32	### 1. Native forms: the record-type registry (REQ-S05-001, REQ-S05-006)
33	
34	`form_record_type` (`0068`, read-only for `mth_app`) lists the native forms: code, kind, verbatim title, source reference, the typed table that stores the records (with a discriminator for T04/T16 on `decision.kind`), the write permission that authorizes record writes, whether it takes extension fields and bulk edits, the extension badge and the feature status. The 33 rows are (FS01):
35	
36	| Kind | Rows | Codes |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| `template` | 15 | T01–T09, T11–T16. T10 (Executive Transformation Dashboard, B0094) is the DG4 dashboard read model, not a form; its layout is the slice A `report_layout`/`dashboard` element and its export is slice F. |
39	| `source_deliverable` | 3 | `charter` (M0146), `tom_canvas` (M0147, `tom_canvas_cell`), `business_case` (M0148) |
40	| `extension` | 12 | the M0149 list, in its order: `evidence`, `baseline`, `value_pool`, `resource_plan` (`resource_demand`), `funding_approval` (`funding_decision`), `procedure_definition` (ADR-0042), `change_request`, `meeting_record` (`meeting`), `corrective_plan` (`corrective_case`), `lesson`, `bau_handover`, `control` |
41	| `product` | 3 | `phase_step` (P4), `launch_plan` and `health_assessment` (`planned`, no table: slice H) |
42	
43	`extension_badge` is true exactly for the twelve M0149 rows (CHECK `form_record_type_badge_is_extension`): the playbook supplies a template only for T1–T16, so every M0149 record is an extension (REQ-S05-006 "an 'extension' badge where the playbook supplies no template"). A `planned` row has no table and takes no extension fields (CHECK `form_record_type_storage_complete`). Titles: templates verbatim from the `source_element` labels (playbook blocks above), M0149 rows verbatim from the M0149 list, source deliverables from M0146–M0148; every Arabic title is marked "(ترجمة مؤقتة)" (provisional translation).
44	
45	**The twelve extension record types are created and read through their existing DG2–DG4 operations** (REQ-S05-006 "all twelve record types can be created and retrieved via the API"): `createEvidence`/`getEvidence`, `createBaseline`/`getBaseline`, `createValuePool`/`getValuePool`, `createResourceDemand`/`getResourceDemand`, `createFundingDecision`/`getFundingDecision`, `putProcedureDefinition`/`getProcedureDefinition` (ADR-0042, new), `createChangeRequest`/`getChangeRequest`, `createMeeting`/`getMeeting`, `createCorrectiveCase`/`getCorrectiveCase`, `createLesson`/`listLessons`, `createBauHandover`/`getBauHandover`, `createControl`/`listControls`. Lessons and controls have no single-record GET in the DG4 contract; they are retrieved through their list operations, which is what the acceptance requires ("retrieved via the API"). The badge is served in `listFormRecordTypes` and `getTransformationFormSchema` (`extensionBadge: true`) and rendered in en and ar by FE-C on each of the twelve forms and in Studio.
46	
47	### 2. Form schema versions and protected source columns (REQ-S05-002, REQ-S06-004)
48	
49	Form schemas are Studio configuration kind `form_schema`, one key **`forms`** (the `ConfigResolver` default key of the kind; ADR-0039 §3). `forms` v1 (`0068`, seed, published) has **no element rows**, so every form resolves to the registry: the DG2–DG4 forms exactly, with no extension field (FS05).
50	
51	`form_source_field` (`0068`, read-only) is the stable-identity registry of the **protected source columns**: 111 rows, one per minimum field of M0129–M0144 (T10 excluded, §1), with `label_en` verbatim from the master-prompt row at `source_ref` (e.g. T03 `gap` = "gap", M0131), a provisional Arabic label, the Studio field type, and where the platform stores it: `column` (one typed column `table.column`; 71 rows, each checked against `information_schema`, FS03), `composite` (several typed columns or related rows) or `computed` (calculated by a DG2–DG4 engine, e.g. T06 "weighted result", T14 "realized").
52	
53	Two element types are added to the `form_schema` kind (`0068` widens the element-type CHECK and redefines `methodology_element_guard()` with every slice A rule kept verbatim):
54	
55	- **`form`** (stable key = a `form_record_type` code): form-level `labelEn/labelAr`, `helpEn/helpAr`. Always `origin = 'source'`, never removed (CHECK `methodology_element_form_fixed`; FE12): a form is neither added nor deleted in Studio.
56	- **`form_field`** (stable key `<recordType>.<fieldKey>`):
57	  - `origin = 'source'` names a `form_source_field` (`methodology_element_source_identity`; FE13). An admin may relabel it, add help and mark it required (FE03). It is **never removed** (CHECK `methodology_element_source_field_protected`; FE04 — this is REQ-S05-002's "attempting to delete the T03 'Gap' column is rejected") and its `fieldType`, when present, must equal the registry type (`methodology_element_source_field_type_fixed`; FE05: "change their type semantics" is refused).
58	  - `origin = 'admin'` is an **extension field**: its key is lowercase `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$`, is not a source column key of the record type, and the record type must allow extension fields (`methodology_element_extension_field_key`; FE06, FE07). It names one of the eleven field types (CHECK `methodology_element_field_type`; FE08) with the settings §3 requires (`methodology_element_field_settings`; FE09, FE10). An extension field may be removed in a draft (`removed = true`); its stored values stay in history and are no longer accepted for that version (§4).
59	- Element writes follow slice A: only in a draft being edited (FE16 after publish), one audit event each (FE14), lock 730250, `If-Match` on the draft. Studio edits use slice A's `putConfigElement`/`removeConfigElement` with `elementType` `form` or `form_field`; the forms kind provider (BE-D, `forms/provider.ts`, registered in `methodology/kinds.ts`) validates the attributes with the Zod schemas of §3 and maps database refusals to the §10 codes. Publish, preview, review where configured, diff, compatibility and rollback are the slice A pipeline unchanged (FE15).
60	- **Diff and compatibility (REQ-S06-007, REQ-S06-008).** The provider lists added, removed and changed fields as diff rows ("the diff lists the added field"); compatibility is `warn` for a new required extension field (pinned transformations stay pinned; ADR-0040's migration preview lists "new required field" from this provider) and `fail` for a calculated field whose formula does not validate.
61	
62	Adding an extension field to T03 and publishing it succeeds (FE02, FE15); this is REQ-S05-002's first clause.
63	
64	### 3. The eleven field types and their server-side validation (REQ-S06-005)
65	
66	Pure validators and normalizers in `packages/shared/src/forms/**` (KBE-B; exported through `@mth/shared/calc`), used by the API for extension-field values and procedure inputs (ADR-0042 §2), and by the web for the same messages. Every value is stored as JSON in the shape below; decimals are **strings**, never JSON numbers.
67	
68	| Type | Settings (attributes) | Accepted input → stored value | Server-side refusal (400 field code) |
69	|---|---|---|---|
70	| `text` | `maxLength` 1–2000 (default 2000) | shared `freeText` rules → string | `validation.text` |
71	| `rich_text` | `maxLength` 1–20000 | the DG2 sanitized rich-text subset → string | `validation.rich_text` |
72	| `number` | `min`, `max` (decimal strings), `scale` 0–6 | decimal string `^-?\d{1,15}(\.\d{1,6})?$` → same string, decimal.js comparison | `validation.decimal` |
73	| `currency` | `currencyCode` (default the transformation currency, SAR), `scale` 0–2 | `{amount: decimal string, currencyCode: ISO 4217 letters}` → same; no float on any path ("a currency field stores decimal SAR without float error") | `validation.currency_amount`, `validation.currency_code` |
74	| `percentage` | `min`, `max` as fractions (default 0–1) | `"12%"`, `"12"` (percent) or the fraction in the API body `"0.12"` is normalized to the **fraction string** `"0.12"` with decimal.js (`12% → 0.12`); the API body carries the fraction | `validation.percentage` |
75	| `date` | `min`, `max` | `YYYY-MM-DD`, a real calendar date, in the transformation timezone (default Asia/Riyadh) | `validation.date` |
76	| `reference` | `targetRecordType` (a `form_record_type` code) | uuid of a record of that type in the same transformation (checked in the transaction) | `validation.reference` |
77	| `attachment` | `maxCount` 1–20 | array of evidence uuids of the same transformation | `validation.attachment` |
78	| `lookup` | `lookupSet` ∈ {`users`, `roles`, `tom_dimensions`, `phases`, `gates`, `currencies`, `business_units`} | the code or id of an active member | `validation.lookup` |
79	| `choice` | `options[]` 1–100 of `{value, labelEn, labelAr}` | one `value` (or an array when `multiple: true`) | `validation.choice` |
80	| `calculated` | `expression` (1–2000), `resultUnitKind` (ADR-0037 N5) | never stored; evaluated at read with `evaluateFormula` over the record's number/currency/percentage fields | definition time: 422 `form_schema.calculated_formula_invalid` |
81	
82	**Calculated fields** use the DG3 formula engine unchanged (`validateFormula`, `evaluateFormula` in `packages/shared/src/formula/**`; no file there changes). The provider validates the expression at element write with the record type's resolved numeric fields as the allowed variables; an unknown variable is refused 422 `form_schema.calculated_formula_invalid` ("a calculated field referencing an unknown field is rejected"). At read, a missing input gives **Not computable** with the missing field named, never 0 (§7).
83	
84	### 4. Custom-field values (REQ-S16-010; amends ADR-0014 §4)
85	
86	Extension-field values live in **`form_custom_value`** (`0068`): one row per record (`UNIQUE (record_type, record_id)`; CV12), with `transformation_id`, the `form_schema_version_id` they were validated against, `field_values` (JSON object ≤ 64 KiB), P2 stamps and `version`. Core entity columns stay typed and unchanged; no DG2–DG4 table gets a column.
87	
88	*Amendment of ADR-0014 §4 (documented reason):* a side table instead of a `custom_field_values` column on each register table, because a column would put new writes on DG2–DG4 tables whose frozen-column, append-only or immutability triggers (Context 2) would refuse them or would have to be reopened. The side table is additive and keeps every DG2–DG4 trigger unchanged.
89	
90	Validation happens **before persistence** in the API (`forms/custom-values.ts`, BE-D): the record type's write permission and scope; the version = `ConfigResolver.pinnedVersion(transformationId, 'form_schema')`; each key an active extension field of the record type in that version; each value validated by §3; required extension fields present; calculated fields not accepted. The database repeats the structural part as the last line of defence (trigger `form_custom_value_guard` and `p5_form_record_ref_guard`):
91	
92	- the version equals the transformation's `form_schema` pin, or forms v1 when there is no pin (`form_custom_value_pinned_version`; CV01, CV09);
93	- every key is an `admin`, not removed `form_field` of the record type in that version (`form_custom_value_unknown_field`; CV01, CV08);
94	- every non-null value has its type's JSON shape: decimal strings for number and percentage, `{amount, currencyCode}` with exactly those two keys for currency, `YYYY-MM-DD` for date, a uuid for reference, an array of at most 20 items for attachment, strings for text/rich text/lookup/choice; a calculated value is refused (`form_custom_value_type_shape`; CV05, CV06, CV07); JSON null clears a value (CV15);
95	- the record exists in the transformation, of the right T04/T16 kind (`form_custom_value_record_ref`; CV10); record type and id never change (`form_custom_value_record_fixed`; CV11);
96	- P2 guards: version +1 (CV14), audit at COMMIT (CV13).
97	
98	The decimal shape check proves REQ-S06-005's storage clauses at the database: `"0.12"` for 12 % and `"1500000.10"` SAR are stored and read back exactly (CV03, CV04).
99	
100	**Pins.** A transformation without a `form_schema` pin resolves to forms v1 (ADR-0039 §3, "never the latest"), so every DG1–DG4 transformation keeps the DG4 forms (G04: no pin is back-filled). A transformation **created after this release** is pinned to the newest published `forms` version in its create transaction: BE-D registers a `TransformationInitializer` (port wired by BE-A in `server.ts`) that inserts the `form_schema` pin with its audit event; DG1's `createTransformation` request and response are unchanged. Moving an existing transformation to a newer forms version is a methodology migration (ADR-0040; M0155).
101	
102	### 5. The common form framework (REQ-S05-001)
103	
104	All operations are scoped `/transformations/{transformationId}/form-records/{recordType}/…` with `recordType` a `form_record_type` code (planned types → 422 `form_record.type_planned`), so one implementation serves every native form; the existing register routes stay byte-stable.
105	
106	| Capability | Design |
107	|---|---|
108	| **Inline help** | `getTransformationFormSchema` returns, for the pinned version, every field (source and extension, ordered) with resolved labels and help in en and ar, type, settings, `required`, `protected` (source) and `extension` flags, and the form's badge. FE-C renders help beside each field and translates at render time. |
109	| **Validation** | Server-side: the existing register validation for source columns (unchanged) and §3/§4 for extension fields; the web runs the same pure validators for immediate messages; one form-level alert per form. |
110	| **Draft saving** | `form_draft` (`0068`): the author's partial request body (`payload` ≤ 256 KiB) for a new record or an existing one (with its `base_record_version`). `open → closed` (`saved` after the record write succeeded, or `discarded`); a closed draft never changes (FD05, FD06); one open draft per user and existing record (FD02); the owner is the creator (FD03); planned record types refused (FD04). Only the owner reads its drafts (others get 404). "A saved draft reopens" = `getFormDraft` returns the stored payload; when the record's version moved past `base_record_version`, the response says so (`baseChanged: true`) and the client offers the §5 conflict view. |
111	| **Version history** | `listFormRecordVersions` reads `audit_event` for `(record_type = table, record_id)` ordered by `seq`: each entry has `newVersion`, actor, time, action and the changed field names from `changes`. No back-fill and no new table (p5-plan §3 row 6). A new version appears in history because every register write already writes its audit event (ADR-0004). |
112	| **Comments** | `form_record_comment` (`0068`): append-only (FC04, FC05), body 1–4000 (free-text rules), one reply level on the same record (FC02, FC03), audited (FC06), record in the same transformation (FC07). |
113	| **Attachments** | Evidence links. For the twenty record types of the DG2 `evidence_link` (T01–T04, T16, charter, TOM canvas, baseline, value pool, …) the operations read and write `evidence_link` unchanged; for all other record types they use `form_record_attachment` (`0068`), which refuses the `evidence_link` types (`form_record_attachment_use_evidence_link`; FA03) so each record type has exactly one attachment place (M0150). `active → removed` with a reason (FA05, FA06), only the removal columns change (FA04), one active link per evidence and record (FA02). |
114	| **Permissions** | Reads: `transformation.read` in scope (and the register's own read rule where stricter). Writes: the record type's `write_permission_code` in scope, re-checked at commit time. Comments: `form_record.comment`. |
115	| **Bulk editing where suitable** | `bulkUpdateFormRecords`: 1–100 items `{recordId, version, sourceFields?, customFieldValues?}`, all-or-nothing in one transaction; allowed only where `form_record_type.bulk_edit_allowed` (422 `form_record.bulk_not_allowed`) and only for source columns marked `bulk_editable` (owner, due dates, impact/probability/stance, confidence; 422 `form_record.bulk_field_not_editable`). Each item goes through the register's own update function (same validation, audit and events as a single edit). Any stale item → 409 `form_record.bulk_conflict` listing `{recordId, currentVersion}` and nothing is saved. |
116	| **Export** | `exportFormRecords` (`text/csv` or `application/json`; at most 5000 rows, else 422 `form_export.too_large`): the source columns of `column` storage plus the extension fields of the pinned version, header labels in the requested language, decimals as strings, Unknown as an empty cell plus a `<field>_status` column (`unknown`/`not_computable`), never 0. CSV is RFC 4180 UTF-8 with BOM (Arabic in Excel). Large and formatted exports are slice F. |
117	| **Recoverable conflict** | Every P5 write with a stale `If-Match` returns 409 `form_record.conflict` with `currentVersion` and the current representation, so FE-C shows "theirs vs yours" and re-applies the user's changes on the current version. The DG2–DG4 register routes keep their own 409 codes; FE-C's conflict view re-reads the record with its GET on any 409 (no change to those routes). |
118	
119	### 6. State machines
120	
121	```text
122	form_draft:              open -> closed (closed_reason 'saved' | 'discarded'); closed is final
123	form_record_attachment:  active -> removed; removed is final
124	form_record_comment:     append-only (no state)
125	form_custom_value:       one mutable row per record; version +1 per write
126	form_schema versions:    the slice A machine (ADR-0039 §1), unchanged
127	```
128	
129	### 7. Decimal and Unknown semantics
130	
131	Number, currency and percentage values are decimal strings validated and compared with decimal.js and stored as JSON strings (CV03–CV05); percentages are fractions (`0.12`), shown as `12 %` at render; currency always carries its code, default the transformation currency (SAR). A field with no value is **Unknown** (blank with "Unknown" in en/ar), never 0. A calculated field with a missing or Unknown input is **Not computable** with the missing field named, never 0 or green. The export marks both (§5). Counts are integers.
132	
133	### 8. Locks, events, jobs
134	
135	No new lock: custom values, drafts and attachments are single rows guarded by `If-Match` and the P2 version step; comments are append-only inserts (ordering by `created_at, id`). **730255 stays reserved** (p5-plan §4 offered it for a comment thread "only if the ADR shows a need"; it shows none). Studio element writes use 730250/730251 (slice A). Outbox events (schema_version 1): `form_record.custom_values_updated` `{recordType, recordId, version}`, `form_record.commented` `{recordType, recordId, commentId}` (for slice E notifications). No job.
136	
137	### 9. Authorization (permissions matrix §19)
138	
139	`P5_FORMS_PROCEDURES_PERMISSIONS` (`0070`; seed test; PM01): `form_record.comment` (write: SP, TL, BO, WL, FIN, TO, KDS, TD, CM). Everything else reuses existing codes:
140	
141	| Operation group | Permission | Notes |
142	|---|---|---|
143	| list record types, admin form schema | `methodology.read` | AUD reads |
144	| Studio field edits (slice A element operations) | `methodology.configure` (ADM_METHOD); publish `methodology.publish`; review `methodology.review` (TO, never the author) | slice A rules |
145	| transformation form schema, versions, comments list, attachments list, drafts list, export | `transformation.read` in scope | AUD reads; drafts: own only |
146	| custom values, drafts, attachments, bulk | the record type's `write_permission_code` in scope | e.g. T03 `tom.edit`, T14 `benefit.edit`, funding `funding.approve` (a business approval code, held by SP: only the approver annotates a funding decision) |
147	| comment | `form_record.comment` + read scope | |
148	
149	AUD holds no write code here and gets 403 on every write. ADM_METHOD, ADM_TECH and ADM_ACCESS hold no business-approval or finance code (0005 trigger), configure forms only through Studio, and hold no register write permission, so a methodology admin cannot edit business records through the form framework. No SoD rule beyond the registers' own applies (comments and drafts approve nothing).
150	
151	### 10. Refusal codes and English texts (exact)
152	
153	| Status | Code | English text (exact) |
154	|---|---|---|
155	| 422 | `form_schema.source_column_protected` | Source columns cannot be deleted. Relabel the column or add help instead. |
156	| 422 | `form_schema.source_column_type_fixed` | The type of a source column cannot be changed. |
157	| 422 | `form_schema.extension_key_invalid` | An extension field needs a new key of lowercase letters, digits and underscores that is not a source column. |
158	| 422 | `form_schema.extensions_not_allowed` | This form does not take extension fields. |
159	| 422 | `form_schema.field_type_unknown` | Choose one of the eleven field types. |
160	| 422 | `form_schema.field_settings_invalid` | This field type is missing a required setting. |
161	| 422 | `form_schema.calculated_formula_invalid` | The calculated field's formula is invalid or refers to an unknown field. |
162	| 422 | `form_schema.form_fixed` | Native forms cannot be added or removed. |
163	| 422 | `form_record.type_planned` | This form is not available in this release. |
164	| 422 | `form_record.custom_field_unknown` | This field is not an extension field of this form in the version your transformation uses. |
165	| 422 | `form_record.custom_field_required` | Fill in the required extension fields. |
166	| 409 | `form_record.conflict` | This record changed since you opened it. Review the current version, then apply your changes again. |
167	| 422 | `form_record.bulk_not_allowed` | Bulk editing is not available for this form. |
168	| 422 | `form_record.bulk_field_not_editable` | This field cannot be bulk edited. |
169	| 422 | `form_record.bulk_too_many` | Edit at most 100 records at a time. |
170	| 409 | `form_record.bulk_conflict` | One of the selected records changed. Nothing was saved; reload and try again. |
171	| 422 | `form_export.too_large` | This export has more than 5000 rows. Narrow the filter or use a report export. |
172	| 422 | `form_draft.closed` | This draft is closed. Start a new draft. |
173	| 409 | `form_draft.open_exists` | You already have an open draft of this record. Continue it or discard it first. |
174	| 422 | `form_attachment.evidence_unknown` | Choose evidence from this transformation. |
175	| 422 | `form_attachment.already_removed` | This attachment is already removed. |
176	| 422 | `form_comment.parent_invalid` | A reply must answer a top-level comment on the same record. |
177	| 400 field | `validation.text` | Enter text within the allowed length. |
178	| 400 field | `validation.rich_text` | Enter formatted text within the allowed length. |
179	| 400 field | `validation.decimal` | Enter a number within the allowed range, with at most the allowed decimals. |
180	| 400 field | `validation.currency_amount` | Enter an amount with at most two decimals. |
181	| 400 field | `validation.currency_code` | Enter a three-letter currency code. |
182	| 400 field | `validation.percentage` | Enter a percentage within the allowed range, for example 12%. |
183	| 400 field | `validation.date` | Enter a valid date as YYYY-MM-DD. |
184	| 400 field | `validation.reference` | Choose an existing record of the expected type in this transformation. |
185	| 400 field | `validation.attachment` | Choose evidence from this transformation (at most the allowed number). |
186	| 400 field | `validation.lookup` | Choose an active value from the list. |
187	| 400 field | `validation.choice` | Choose one of the listed options. |
188	
189	Missing `If-Match` → 428 and stale on non-form operations → 409 with the ADR-0007 standard codes; AUD and missing permission → 403 `auth.forbidden`; outside scope → 404.
190	
191	## Alternatives considered
192	
193	1. **A `custom_field_values jsonb` column on every register table (ADR-0014 §4 wording).** Rejected: new writes on DG2–DG4 tables with frozen-column, append-only or immutability triggers (`funding_decision`, `evidence`, `decision`) would need those triggers reopened; the side table needs none (§4 amendment).
194	2. **One form schema key per record type.** Rejected: `transformation_config_pin` is unique per `(transformation, kind)` (`0011`), so a transformation could pin only one of them; one `forms` key keeps one pin per kind and one migration path.
195	3. **Extension fields as typed columns created by DDL at publish.** Rejected: runtime DDL from the application role contradicts ADR-0003 (no DDL by `mth_app`) and makes rollback destructive.
196	4. **Refusing deletion of a source column only in the API.** Rejected: REQ-S16-010 and M0154 "protect … core data invariants" ask for the database as the last line of defence (FE04).
197	5. **A new attachments table for every record type.** Rejected: it would duplicate `evidence_link` for the twenty DG2 types (M0150).
198	6. **Adding `customFieldValues` to the existing register request bodies.** Rejected: P1–P4 paths stay byte-stable except the D-142 extensions; a separate operation is additive.
199	
200	## Consequences
201	
202	- Every native form gets drafts, history, comments, attachments, export, bulk edit where suitable and a recoverable conflict through one set of P5 operations; the DG2–DG4 register routes are unchanged.
203	- Existing transformations keep forms v1 until a migration; new ones are pinned to the newest published forms version at creation (BE-D initializer).
204	- `methodology_element_guard()` now also guards `form_schema` elements; every slice A rule is kept (the ARCH-01 integration suite must stay green).
205	- The DG4 export of a register (if any) is unchanged; the P5 export is additive.
206	
207	## Verification
208	
209	- **Database (probe, real output):** G00–G05, FS01–FS05, FE01–FE16, CV00–CV15, FD01–FD07, FC01–FC07, FA01–FA06, PM01 (`probe-output.txt`, 116/116 PASS with ADR-0042's probes).
210	- **API (implementer tests, p5-work-split §B):** T01 and T14 literal (REQ-S05-001): a saved draft reopens; after an edit, history lists the new version; a comment and an attachment persist; export returns the rows; a second save with the old `If-Match` returns the recoverable 409 with `currentVersion`. REQ-S05-002: adding an extension field to T03 publishes; deleting T03 `gap` → 422 `form_schema.source_column_protected`. REQ-S06-005: `12%` stores `"0.12"`; `1500000.10` SAR reads back exactly; a calculated field naming an unknown field → 422 `form_schema.calculated_formula_invalid`. REQ-S16-010: a value violating its schema → 400/422 before persistence and the database refuses it too. REQ-S05-006: the twelve types are created and read through the operations of §1, and their forms show the badge in en and ar. AUD 403 on every write; `If-Match` 428/409; one audit event per mutation; commit-time re-authorization.
211
